New raw `raw/stripe-radar-how-radar-works-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-radar-how-it-works-2026.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-radar-how-it-works.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/radar/how-radar-works`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: https://docs.stripe.com/radar/how-radar-works says Stripe Radar protects against transaction fraud, account risk, and customer abuse. Radar screens successful, declined, blocked and review-flagged payment attempts against supported methods, and excludes non-card SetupIntents (new raw lines 9–13, old raw lines 8–20). November provides four plan choices and three matrices. All four have essential card fraud prevention, card-testing prevention, and alerts. Standard and above add expanded prevention, supported-method coverage, analytics, default rules/lists and risk levels. Plus and above add transaction risk scores, custom rules/backtests/lists, manual reviews, risk preferences, Adaptive 3DS, Smart Refunds, Assistant, advanced analytics and agentic insights; dynamic transaction thresholds are Pro. Stripe reports a 42% average improvement for Standard versus Lite (new raw lines 15–46). Pro has the trial, bot, multi-account, account sharing and pay-as-you-go customer abuse controls. Standard and above have account AI prevention, analytics, default rules/lists, reviews, recommendations, fraudulent merchant signal, history and risk levels; Plus and Pro add account scores, customization, dynamic reserves, fraudulent website signal, Assistant and agentic insights (new raw lines 48–76). Stripe charges Standard, Plus and Pro when it screens an authorization or charge, including one-offs, recurrent payments, invoices and subscription lifecycle events. For Stripe Billing subscriptions, Radar screens and charges on initial payment and first payment after a method change. Merchants can configure a count of successful renewals to screen. After those it skips renewals without charging, restarting at the next payment on a changed method before reapplying the configured skip behavior. On free trials the first screen is when the buyer is charged. Stripe charges the Connect account fee to the platform and the screened transaction at the collecting account’s rate. A collecting platform can reduce the subsequent transfer to pass through fees (new raw lines 78–84). source-stripe-radar-how-it-works.md reflects the May capture's three labels, account fee, first-transaction-only Billing exception, inline payment-method list/preview and feature bullets (old raw lines 8–36). Its undated presentation needs the November segmentation and fees.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/how-radar-works, the 2026-11-07 plan/feature tables and subscription and Connect fee rules are substantive (new raw lines 15–76 and 78–84). Preserve the May 2026-05-10 names and terms (old raw lines 8–10 and 22–36) in source-stripe-radar-how-it-works.md and maintain both raw source links. Do not infer a plan rename, plan equivalence, grandfathering, an effective date or an exact fee from the change. May's cards/card-backed wallets/ACH/SEPA and additional-method preview (old raw lines 12–20 and 36) contrast with November's all-supported-methods handoff (new raw lines 11–13). The handoff changes the route for determining coverage. Linked method details are not a universal GA statement: the November matrix places all-method protection and expanded controls at Standard or above, and the same-date supported-methods companion lines 9–17 also scopes default high-risk controls and describes possible Lite blocking. Both capture dates exclude non-card SetupIntents within the overview; distinguish the concept's separate settings caveat. Separate the earlier scoring/rules statement in the Risk Evaluation route from the newer screening/fee model. The switch from feature bullets to comparison tables carries substantive entitlement evidence; heading spacing, link/fragment destinations and the discovery metadata have no independent product-behavior meaning. Update the Stripe Radar concept’s plan/pricing/method sections and its reciprocal source backlink at line 252. Preserve Related Pages links from the summary to Stripe Radar, Stripe Declines and 3D Secure and the concept's supported-methods, risk-evaluation and platform source routes. Refresh the Stripe index source entry at line 508, reachable through wiki/index.md line 7, and retain its Stripe Radar concept entry at line 719.
